420602.overview:
A native port of Dark Forces based on The Force Engine. In it you are Kyle Katarn, a former Imperial officer turned mercenary, now hired by the Rebel Alliance. After having stolen the Death Star plans from a remote facility, he is tasked with investigating the sudden destruction of a hidden Rebel base. This leads him to face off against Imperial General Rom Mohc and the various iterations of his Dark Troopers - cybernetic soldiers with the armor and firepower to turn the tide of the war.

Dark Forces is a close prequel to the original Star Wars movie trilogy. The game marks LucasArts' first attempt to enter the first-person shooter market. Instead of licensing the DOOM engine, like many competitors, LucasArts created its own internal Jedi engine. The Jedi engine contains advanced features over similar tech, including the ability to look up and down, jump, crouch, and limited support (in the build used for Dark Forces) for rooms (sectors) over rooms. The 3D models also make occasional appearances inside the game, as turrets or Kyle's ship dropping him off or picking him up from each mission.

Most levels have a fairly complex, often maze-like structure, and include various switches that need to be activated to change the layout of the level. Jumping is integrated into the gameplay, as certain areas can only be accessed in that way. In addition to weapons, Kyle can use shields to protect himself from damage, a head lamp to illuminate dark areas, as well as specific items used to counter environmental hazards. The player character is given a certain amount of "lives" per level; he dies permanently once he runs out of all of them. Game progress can be saved only between missions.

The game features fourteen substantial levels as Kyle works to disarm the Dark Trooper project. Many levels reference characters or areas from the Star Wars movie trilogy, such as a visit with Jabba the Hutt, a trip to Coruscant, and a battle through the interior of a Star Destroyer. As opposed to most first-person shooters of the time period, every level has objectives for Kyle to complete, ranging from grabbing a clue and getting out alive, to planting charges around a facility to demolish it. Cutscenes appear between key missions to update the plot.

420712.overview: A cool vampire-hunting game inspired by Castlevania (or maybe MSX Vampire Killer: keys for doors?) but also has a gun (like in Aria of Sorrow) to take out the baddies.

420735.overview: What do you get if you mix the game play and in part, the graphics of The Bitmap Brothers classic 'Gods'; a Platformer from 1991, with a futuristic shooter? You'd probably get the "unreleased" Amiga game ' Desolate World '. But is this truly an unreleased game, many of you probably haven't heard of it, but we can tell you this was a demo coverdisk version released as public in a Czech magazine Amiga Review 28!

420739.overview: A doom style first person shooter written in ASM 68k in 1995 by Alex Amsel, Allister Brimble and Richard Whittall.

420852.overview: This story took place in the land of Thalax, during the reign of the wise King Duncan. It was a time of peace and prosperity and life few quiet all over the realm...until the Demons awoke from their millenarian oblivion!

420854.overview: An unfinished Xevious clone created by Claudio Mazzuco in 1997.

420855.overview: Demo released in 1996 and then later as part of the The AGA Experience Volume 3. It is a Bomberman style game created by Fully Bugged Software.

420868.overview: A colorful genre mix of elements from science fiction, fantasy and our earth, mashed together and amalgamated into a lovely RPG by the SOMS-Team. Never released as it could not match the speed of processing with the hardware target they desired, but a good play for the patient, the emulated and those with powerful systems.

420956.overview: A Czech Republic, first person RPG dungeon crawler. The first Czech game of the Multis group, which could be described as a mix of dungeon and adventure with a historical theme, a large amount of humor and surprising twists during the game.

421046.overview: The object of Deface is to remove all of the tiles. You do so by matching two tiles on the outer left & right edges of the puzzle. There are four layers of tiles and the edge tile from one layer can be matched with an edge tile of another layer.

421354.overview:
Der Schatz im Silbersee is a graphic adventure game with an icon-based point-and-click interface.

Based on the novel Der Schatz im Silbersee by German author Karl May, this game let’s you join the wild west adventurers Old Firehand, chief Winnetou and Tante Droll on their way up the Arkansas River, through Utah to the Rocky Mountains. They’re searching for the famous treasure in Silver Lake, but they’re not the only ones: the unscrupulous Red Colonel and his band of tramps aren’t exactly eager to share...

You take control of Old Firehand, performing actions with a set of only three basic commands and a good deal of inventory management. The game features four episodes: the steamer Dogfish, the rafter’s camp, Butler’s farm, and the treasure hunt at the Silbersee. The Eagle’s Tail and Utah chapters of the novel, roughly one half of the book, are omitted. The cast is greatly reduced, too, with neither Old Shatterhand nor any of the companions appearing at all. Knowledge of the book will not give you any advantages, as all of the puzzles are original and often deviate strongly from the events in the novel.

You can find more information on Karl May and his books in the trivia and links sections.

421838.overview: The idea of the game is to destroy the opponent. This is accomplished when their energy level decreases to zero. The energy bars are white, the velocity bars are blue.

421841.overview: A single player point and click adventure game created by Locus Design in 1992 and released as Shareware.

421866.overview: An AMOS based freeware game created by Shadow Software (Aaron Fothergill) in 1991. In the game, you control Arnold Shortscribbler, who is trying to write an article for the next AMOS newsletter. Unfortunately, he has only a limited amount of time to collect together all his AMOS P.D. collection to allow him to write the article. Arnold must avoid muggers, rottweilers , pit bulls, water and an occasional mutant pigeon while gathering his collection. Use spades to trap baddies, use stop signs to stop muggers.

421883.overview: A German text/image based adventure game. The adventures of a castaway on a deserted isle. You open your eyes and see a bright blue pond in which tiny kayaks are busy making their way. As you try to stand up, you feel every muscle in your body rebel. You remember wanting to travel using a small sailing boat to relax completely before the festival. After a few days on the open sea, bad weather arrived. The tiny ship was tossed. If only there were more crew than you! Now you are stuck here, but that isn't half bad. You'd be thankful if one of these huts had some food. Hopefully you can still make it to the festival!

421884.overview: Drop bombs on the buildings to blow them up, otherwise you will crash into them and die. An AMOS based game created by Roger North and published by Courbois Software in 1991. DEMOLITION MISSION was originally a licenceware game of the same name written in AMOS (incl. source code) and released on Berliner Spielekiste Disk #113 in 1990. That same year it was distributed outside Germany by various PD software libraries also (e.g. 17-Bit PD Disk #1747, Assassins PD Disk #688). Several months later, however, the Dutch language was added to the game and, ultimately, it was published commercially by Courbois Software during 1991.

421886.overview: A mind-scrambling two player demo presented by The Activas Washing Corporation. Programmed by Dave Mentos, Graphics by T.C, this is a shooter where you drive your machine-gun equipped jeep to the battlefield and shoot your way to victory. Enemy soldiers may also be disabled by running them over, but don't try that with a tank!

421887.overview: A bunny themed shooter from Martin Button, released to PD in 1996.

421890.overview: Take part as a Helicopter in this single player shoot-em-up game which was released as shareware by Micro Acid Software in 1994. Each mission gives you objectives to complete, then you can try to make it home alive. Pick up power ups to become more deadly and effective.

421891.overview: A shareware horror shooter game created with 3D Construction Kit by Tony Hartley in 1996. A creepy FPS game which starts outside a graveyard.

421893.overview: Use the mouse to collect various diamonds and items on the screen in this freeware game by Harshy Wanigasekara from 1992.

421939.overview: An AMOS based freeware conversion of the ST game similar to that of Boulderdash, created by the original ST programmers, the Happening Boiz in 1991. Dizzy Lizzy is a Boulder Dash clone where you guide Dizzy on his quest to collect diamonds. On every level you have to collect all of the diamonds before you may continue to the next level. You have to watch out for boulders, Wayne (who will only move when you stand still), dynamite and bombs. Bombs does not go off the moment they hit an obstacle, you have about five moves before they detonate. After a bomb detonates a large area becomes impassible, so the player has to be careful not to get trapped.

421945.overview: A 1992 freeware game from Dave Krohne likely written on a D.A.R.E. where you must avoid abusive substances and blast them when you can.

421952.overview: A freeware German text/RPG adventure game from Christian Heitzer to get you fired up.

421953.overview:
Dungeon of Nadroj is a shareware dungeon-crawler inspired by games such as Hack, Larn, Moira, Shadowgate, Blackmar's Dungeon etc (according to the intro text). Using the numeric keypad, you control your adventurer in a six-level dungeon, with the goal of surviving and reaching the bottom floor where you must kill an evil wizard. Four players may play, choosing from four character classes: human, dwarf, elf and hobbit.

The screen is made up of three "windows": an overhead map in traditional Hack fashion, a view of whatever monster, treasure or shop you encounter, and a bottom text window where messages scroll by. Monster encounters offer the choice of attacking, defending, running, thrusting or using items. If you flee, you may be forced to drop something in your inventory. If you encounter a human, dwarf or hobbit you may fight or talk, which may lead to valuable hints.

The full version has a random dungeon generator.

421956.overview: A soundless dungeon crawler for the Amiga made by J.Beckmann and U.Krumnack and dropped in 1990. The goal is to make your way out of the dungeon, avoid or escape prison and reach the monster infested town, while scrapping all the way. Alternative to the original (DungeomM...). Free your small town from occupation by intergalactic mega-bubbles. There are many dungeons to explore and puzzles to solve, and you're sure to encounter some unusual problems. Excellent graphics and animation make this game a PD hit. Continuous mouse control and completely German language.

421962.overview: A challenging shoot-em-up freeware game made in SEUCK by VSC Productions in 1995. Grab the coins, shoot the enemies and the bricks and go as far as your little duck feet can carry you.

421965.overview: An arcade style one on one fighting game created by Interstel and released as a public domain game in 1989.

421968.overview: Play as the FBI in this adventure\shooter by Av Ragnar Yri and John Everett, published by Courbois Software in 1989. Named Prijs Schieten in the Dutch release.

421983.overview: An AMOS based freeware, icon driven RPG game by Frank Otto and made in 1995.

421998.overview:
A new type of real time role-playing adventure unlike anything you have played before! Based on the famous NEC PC-88, MSX series of games, this Amiga port by hitchhikr was made in 2023. Dragon Slayer is commonly considered one of the progenitors of the action RPG genre. The premise is similar to Roguelikes: the player takes control of a knight who must fight his way through large overhead maze-like dungeons. Unlike roguelikes, the combat in the game is fully action-oriented: the player must approach the monster and "bump" into it in order to inflict damage, at the same time trying to avoid its blows. Combat takes place on the same screen as the exploration; monsters will also sometimes pursue the knight if he attempts to escape. Also contrary to roguelikes, none of the locations or items in the game is randomized.

The player can collect power stones and coins during the journey; the power stones increase the hero's strength, while the coins increase his hit points (health). Defeating enemies also yields experience points, which determine the amount of maximum HP the hero is able to receive. The knight is able to cast magic spells, though they are mostly used outside of combat, for example breaking walls, teleporting, or creating a map of the area.

422057.overview: Dragon simulator is a freeware flight sim with a difference. It uses graphics like Wing Commander to present a one to one duel between two dragons, one being computer control. There are 20 levels to play and it gets more difficult with each one. You opponent will grow faster, and more maneuverable. The evil wizard Mangoth has ruled the black forest for centuries. This has caused great suffering for those who dwell on the edge of the woods. You were sent to kill him, caught and turned into one of his dragon-slaves. Now you must fight the 20 dragons of the wizard or they will kill you and destroy your village.

422296.overview: A solitaire strategy game version of the card game Demon, created as shareware by Peter Wiseman and released in 1995. Activating the shareware game gave more card sets, graphics and sound effects and other solitaire games like Klondike.

422298.overview: An icon driven adventure game created with the 3D Construction Kit by Dez Hoyle and Shad-Art in 1993.

422498.overview:
Devils nightshade is a game made in AMOS inspired by ZX Spectrum Atic Atac
This is my first full game made in 1995, never been released before...

422561.overview: Deutsch Tester is an educational program for learning German. The test can be taken with or without a score, from German to Polish and vice versa. The player has the ability to edit and add new tests.

422825.overview: A German-language, shareware adventure game published by Scum Amiga Software using AMOS in 1996.

422835.overview: An AMOS based adventure game from Scum Amiga Software in 1994.

422859.overview: This great pinball machine offers pinball fun for 1 to 4 players. Conquer the 2 game levels and put your skills to the test. Sure, it's something of a classic, but it's still one of the most addictive pinball machines we've ever played. You have to put your pinball skills to the test in 2 game levels with different game images. Pinball kings can of course immortalize themselves by name. 1-4 players can compete against each other.

422905.overview: Die Quelle von Naroth is a shareware party-based role playing game. The mission is to fight an evil wizard which tries to weaken the land of Naroth by drain the land's most important water source. The game features a 3d view with step based movement and a tactical combat system. It's German language only.

422946.overview: D_Solve Crossword is a crossword puzzle game from David Smith, released as freeware in 1993. Includes a nice solver.

422975.overview: A single player, vertically scrolling space shooter from Blank Monks in 1993.

422985.overview: A freeware game from Lee Hurley Productions, made in 2011 based on the TV show of the same name. A contestant chooses one briefcase from a selection of 26. Each briefcase contains a cash value from $0.01 to $1,000,000. Over the course of the game, the contestant eliminates cases from the game, periodically being presented with a "deal" from The Banker to take a cash amount to quit the game. Should the contestant refuse every deal, they are given the chance to trade the case they chose at the outset for the only one left in play at the time; they then win the amount in the selected case.

422986.overview: An F1 Licenseware fantasy themed real-time strategy game created in Blitz BASIC by Malcolm and Lee Bamber and released in 1996. A small war game where you have 4 worlds to fight and each world has 21 towns. Capture all the towns on any world, you capture a town by ordering your army to attack an winning in this game that plays like a primitive Warcraft 2. You can create additional armies as long as you have enough funds to support them.

422987.overview: Rearrange the puzzle sections to make the image match the exemplar on the right Game created by Digital Fx Entertainment and published as licenseware in 1996. Various data\image disks for the game were also available.

422992.overview: A dinosaur themed platform jumper from Ugur Ozyilmazel in 1991 originally, at the time this game was written for Turkish television. Dinozorus, the legendary television game that left its mark on the 1990s.

423030.overview: A single player hamburger shooter from Brian Conrad. Shoot the ketchup at the waves of burgers, fries, dogs and other fast food.

423131.overview: A one or two player competitive bat and ball game that is an amped up version of Pong masquerading as a sport of the future.

423138.overview: This simple demo shows off a small maze with texture mapped walls, which can be navigated with the mouse or joystick. The use of the Doom “hand and gun” sprite gives the engine a familiar feel.

423140.overview: Fly your dragon and battle other dragons in this vertically scrolling  shooter made by Bode Games using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit.

423141.overview: A shoot em up game made in SEUCK by Joe Angell in 1990. Take part as a flying floppy disk!

423374.overview: A hide and seek adventure game where you find the Easter eggs. Contains several mini games including breakout, Tetris and more.  This was an experiment into Amiga development and vector graphics. It wasn't intended to be a commercial game but only the author held a copy and it would otherwise have been lost.

423526.overview: Maybe Dex-Tris would have been more descriptive. This is a single player, freeware Tetris clone from Gary Lee in 1990.

423536.overview: A quite well known and nicely made turn based role-playing game set in the land of Cordovan. As Member of the Adventurer Guild take the challenge on your own, the seven magical jewels have been divided by evil forces and the country no longer protected.  As expected, the player is able to adventure with the most diverse characters supported to choose from. Find the precious stones in imaginative adventures  set in an open world. Friends of this genre will enjoy hours and days of play.

423571.overview: The last attack of the Emz on Matička Zeni. You are standing at the site of the shipwreck. It is the dead of night and everything seems so dark and gloomy. The torn pieces of the bodies of those fellow travelers are lying all around. The pilot's torso is pinned to the ground by the propeller blade. That's probably how he'd like to be found if you could still ask him. There is forest all around. You can go either way. You see the wreckage, the bodies and the pilot. What will you do in this Czech language text adventure by Crudesys from 2009.

423619.overview: A one or two player SEUCK based game from Bode Software, created in 1987 and published by Software 2000. Blast away at dragon's and Dalek and other baddies like copters, trains and pick up red cross for bonus.

423657.overview:
Der blaue Kristall is an ufinished text adventure game for Commodore Amiga computers. Created with AmigaBASIC and MaxonBASIC. In the distant future, the continued existence of the human race is in grave danger. Uncanny diseases, which were previously unknown, are rampant among humans and claim many victims. The plant world mutated and for unknown reasons, a deadly green carpet grows over the land. Fear and terror prevail among the already decimated humanity. It seems as if nature has conspired against man and is now striving to wipe him from the face of the earth for good. A small group of survivors saves themselves on a secluded island in the Saragossa-Sea, where life is still possible without dangers and dangers. 

There the refugees discover the remains of a lost culture. An ancient prophecy has been engraved on the stone tablets, which tells of a blue crystal whose mysterious power could save mankind from destruction. But the only clue to the place where this crystal is said to be is a clue to an underground temple. This chance, however small it may be, must of course not go unused. And so the strongest, bravest and most intelligent is chosen. Thus begins an adventurous odyssey above and below the lonely island, in the vastness of the mysterious Saragossa-Sea.

423682.overview: Drsná cesta meaning, "A rough road" in English. The first part of a trilogy of text adventures, whose creator is Jan Burian alias Utopia from the group Torture. This trilogy of text games consists of three parts called Rough Road, Dark Road and Dead Road.

423697.overview: This is a curious shareware game that plays like a multi player version of the well known game Snake, which looks and plays very similar to Červii. The game title means to Watch the Curve. Like in Snake, you control a "snake" that continuously grows, the object being to stay alive for as long as possible. However unlike Snake, this is by default a multi player game, the object here is to stay in contention the longest. Running into yourself, another players snake, or going out of bounds ends your turn. Players are given points based on how long they last.

423740.overview: An adult sex education game to play with your significant other. Or perhaps it is just e-rotica, The game literally and truthfully classified as a Joystick Waggler by the Hall of Light, which is true on several levels.

423747.overview:
A freeware Czech language text adventure from Pinware in 1995. You see something falling, you try to jump, but you're not fast enough. One of your feet slips and before you can recover, a huge, heavy net falls on top of you. It is so heavy that it will pull you to the ground. You panic and in a few seconds you're completely wrapped up in it. You try to get out, but before you can, you see strangely dressed creatures coming. You are trapped!
You can finally see one of them. He's not much taller than you, but his stance and especially his clothes give off something like... You shudder against your wall in fear. He wears a coarsely woven robe with a leather belt, a shirt with handmade wooden buttons, and homemade sandals. His face is grotesque. Ridiculous!
You're sure you found yourself in some kind of masquerade. But why did they catch you in the net? Why?

423766.overview: Ever just want to feel like you are offline? With this Blitz Basic freeware game by Havsoft of Harvard Spring you will be challenged by a game that requires only the skill of patience and timing for the ultimate of high scores. Your eyes will goggle (or is that Google) as you find yourself playing as a dinosaur where you have to jump over every cacti and duck under every bird to beat your previous high score.

423891.overview:
A German language, freeware, single player adventure game including text with still pics. In the game you might fight the Beast as it's evil attempts to return to the land. What at first sight looked like a completely normal werewolf story turned out to be a nightmare with a thousand-year-old secret.

Strange things happen in a remote castle at the end of the 19th century. Blood comes from the taps. A priest disappears without a trace. Horrifying noises at night. Find out the cause of what happened, rummage through the past, seek the truth, kill the ANIMAL.  The game runs in real time, though it can be paused or sped up. Each full hour is announced via sound and text. The characters do not stay in the same place and move around in the castle. When a person is engaged in conversation, a list of tasks and topics can be selected from a menu. A compass on the right side shows available directions.

423935.overview: An AMOS based, German language text adventure created by Michael Mazur and released as freeware in 1993.

423983.overview: Defender of the Moon is a first person shooter. Star base defense system has failed. To prevent the conquest of the planet player takes control of the rocket launcher. The game takes place on a single side-scrolling location. The player's task is to track down and kill all the enemies. A new enemy wave appears on the left side of the screen moving to the right every several seconds. The player moves viewfinder to the right, left, up or down. Invaders must be eliminated before leaving the location. Passing too many aliens end up losing the base. Collecting A letter gives an extra ammo supply, collecting F letter speed up shooting for several second. The game offers a total of five levels.

424033.overview: Eva and Diabolik turn into actors and score a fabulous blow. But an occult royalty has prepared unexpected surprises, one more horrible than the next.  Diabolik was an Amiga arcade 2D adventure game series released in 1993 by Simulmondo, in Europe. Diabolik is a infamous master thief and anti-hero from the (fictional) Italian city of Clerville. His original personal was a more ruthless approach to getting what he wanted, later becoming more of a Robin Hood, type stealing from criminals and restraining from unnecessary violence.

424045.overview: Dylan Dog 12: Il Lungo Addio is an Action Adventure game, developed and published by Simulmondo, which was released in Europe in 1993. The English translation of the title would be The Long Goodbye. Interactive investigators also have a past. And perhaps a past of sea and love, of silent beaches and departing waves. Then maybe the girl was wearing a short sundress and Dylan watched the fringes of her red jerkin flutter and pretended to fix her blond hair better. Then the summer ended and the girl disappeared. And Dylan's hair has grown and the years have passed and the girl returns to Craven one night nd She too is a woman now and Dylan a man. And they will spend a night, a very long night together, a night with us. The past will return and Dylan will help her find her home. We will simulate, a little nosy, their love story while we pretend to look for the town and the house. And we will discover things about Dylan that we don't know, even things we don't want to know. When the memory will build a dream and the dream will be like a dense, poignant simulation to live. While at the end of the night we will wait for the feared "long goodbye" to arrive.

424232.overview: A historical droving strategy simulator. you are the drover on this journey. You must buy animals, hire drivers and take on extra hands. At the journey's end you must sell your stock and pay back the 2000 pounds sterling you have borrowed and pay for the journey's expenses and the 10% interest the gougers at the bank are charging. Will you make your mark, make a fortune or be ruined?

425696.overview: On the 23rd of December I decided to start making a Christmas-themed game from scratch for my Amiga, hoping to have it finished by Christmas day... well, that didn't go according to plan but at least I got a short playable level made before Boxing Day!

425854.overview: Released as a happy new year's present to the Amiga community, a 9 level platform game created by Amiten Games and released on the last day of 2023. Dogi is a dog that lives in a wonderful place, full of lights and lots of fruits and candies. But one day the inhabitants of the wonderland have become selfish and guard all the food. Your mission is to collect all the food and distribute it amongst the kids who do not have enough. Once you have all the fruit on the level you can move on to the next one.

440399.overview: A faithful conversion of the NES classic Duck Hunt for the Commodore Amiga. It was developed by marggines and released on February 11, 2024.

440411.overview: transcode of Donkey Kong arcade version for Amiga

446267.overview:
This is a simulation of droids armed with different weapons that move erratically around in an enclosed arena. The arena has a floor of magnets, where all the droids can stay powered and fight amongst each other. The colored bullets they fire only works on other colored droids, so those droids that have the same color, is on the same team. The player is the decision maker, and has the range of different droids that he can transfer into the arena by simply pressing a number between 1 and 9. The 2 teams have only limited amount of energy to produce new droids, and every droid has good and bad properties. 
 
A freeware game from Joar Berntsen released in 2004. DroidWars 5 is a realtime mix of shoot'em up and action-strategy,
where the 'virtual-life-actors' (droids) do their job independently of your direct controls, as determined by their individual equipment and/or weaponry.

You can -not- control the droids yourself, except in the Solo game type. From 0 to 3 players can play.

446285.overview:
DOOM comes to Amiga devices as a first-person turn-based role playing game, ported by BSzili from the remnants of the mobile game. It incorporates many elements of the original game, but was designed with the limitations of the platform in mind. Instead of giving complete freedom, you move in steps and turn by 90 degrees. You can move as fast as you want, but when a monster appears, the game becomes completely turn-based, both for movement and attacks.

You are a space marine dispatched to a UAC research facility where a distress call was sent out. You start with a limited amount of health, armor and weapons. As you progress and kill monsters, you gain experience and level up to improve health, strength and agility. When engaging in a fight, hits are determined by your statistics, the type of enemy and the weapon you are currently using. Each enemy has a weapon weakness. You can also collect credits to buy upgrades at computer terminals and talk to characters. The story is revealed through conversations with characters and scripted sequences.

Familiar elements in the ten new levels of the game are the textures, the HUD, explosive barrels, health vials, ammo and armor skulls to collect, green, blue, yellow and red key cards, secret areas, and of course the weapons, armor and enemies. Next to the pistol, shotgun, super shotgun, chain-gun, plasma gun, rocket launcher and BFG-9000, there is also an axe to break doors, a fire extinguisher to put out fires and a mystical weapon called Demon Wolf. A dog collar can be used against dog-like creatures.

448107.overview: Just another minesweeper clone made with AMOS. Wait, dedector or detector? The dedector was written by Mayin Tarayicilari in 1996 and published by APM.

448108.overview: A German-language shareware, puzzle game from Aimo Winkelmann and Reik Winklemann, released in 1993 and created with AMOS. A mix of snake and puzzle for one player. You start the game with 5 lives and must quickly move to all the islands in order in the time limit. You must not cross your own path. The more time left when you hit the last island in order, the higher your points.

448132.overview: A top down vertically scrolling shooter for 1 or 2 players (co-op).  Developed by Tim Prior using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit.

448164.overview: Likely intended to piggyback on the immense popularity of Jurassic Park, Dinosaurs Two (and Mass Extinctions) was the second in a two part series of games intended to edu-tain on the subject and timeline of dinosaurs. It was created by Chris Hill of Total Concepts and published by Central Licenseware Register in 1993. Essentially it is a slideshow of great dinosaur pictures with information about them and what was happening in the timeline during their lifespan. Additional information about what was known about the mass extinction of dinosaurs is also available.

448870.overview:
In 2024, deep within the Amazon jungle lies the ancient Temple of Xol'Tan, a place largely ignored by the modern world. Dr. Victor Dangerous, an innovative scientist and adventurer, has recently established a secret research station within the ruins of the temple. He is determined to explore the mysterious energies of the temple and study the unusual creatures that inhabit it.

One evening, as a fierce storm batters the jungle, lightning strikes the main power supply of the station. The station’s electronics fail, and the temple's automatic security protocols are activated. Doors lock shut, and Dr. Dangerous is violently thrown into a deep tunnel beneath the temple.

As Dr. Dangerous recovers from the fall, he finds himself in a shimmering tunnel, illuminated by glowing crystals and mysterious energies. However, the initial wonder is quickly overshadowed by a serious threat. Surrounding him are aggressive creatures that have emerged from the temple's energy. These creatures seem determined to prevent him from exploring the temple and fulfilling his mission.

Dr. Dangerous’ equipment is damaged, and his weapon only functions intermittently. He must confront the attacking creatures, which, with their surprisingly intelligent and coordinated attacks, make survival difficult. Some creatures attack him directly, while others use the environment to trap or overwhelm him.

With his equipment limited and under constant threat, Dr. Dangerous needs to be resourceful. His goal is to find batteries scattered deep within the tunnel, which are essential for restoring his station’s systems. These batteries must be inserted into the station’s computers to deactivate the security protocols and regain control.

As Dr. Dangerous navigates the temple, he learns more about the connection between the creatures and the temple’s energy source. The creatures are not merely obstacles but keys to the temple's secrets. Their aggressive nature is a result of the unstable energy the temple emits, and Dr. Dangerous realizes that controlling this energy is crucial.

With each battery found and each computer repaired, Dr. Dangerous gets closer to his goal. However, working with the temple's energy presents new challenges and dangers. Each time he reaches a new level of the temple, his weapon is reset by the security protocols, forcing him to continuously develop new strategies to defend himself against the creatures.

After a long and strenuous battle, Dr. Dangerous finally locates the last batteries and repairs the remaining computers. The temple’s security system is deactivated, the aggressive energy subsides, and the creatures retreat, allowing the station to return to normal operation.

With control of the station restored and a new understanding of the temple's secrets, Dr. Dangerous returns to civilization.

448988.overview:
Droid is a platform/shooter game created in 1991 by Miles Lord and originally released on ST Format's Issue 37 (August 1992) coverdisk.  Droid Special Edition is a remake of the game which takes advantage of all of the extra hardware features of the Commodore Amiga - blitter, hardware scrolling, sampled sound, enhanced palette and two-button joystick.    
 
You (yes, you - ask your mum) are a droid, and in this game you MUST destroy enemies and collect powerups to blow "up" sort of barriers at the end bit or whatever, to reveal an exit so that you can go to there.

Items

E - increase energy
A - increase ammo
Keycards - use to remove gold/blue/grey barriers
Grenades - use to destroy barriers at the end of the game
Double arrow - refill energy and ammo

Weapons
Single shot - standard weapon
Double shot - twice as powerful as standard weapon
Triple shot - 3-barrel version of standard weapon
Rocket - vertical shot
Bomb - bouncing bomb

Hints

There are areas that are blocked off unless a certain number of items are collected or a certain number of enemies are destroyed.  Look out for messages in the status panel that suggest which parts have been unlocked and use the map to find them.

Energy and ammo items don't necessarily have to be picked up immediately upon sight, return to collect them when they're really needed.

An extra life is awarded every 20,000 points.

449001.overview:
A horse racing game for up to 4 human players by Lothar Maier, released as shareware in 1992. The game is German language and the full version could be ordered from the author. In the simulation game you have the task of managing a horse and increasing the existing starting capital (20,000 DM). You have to try to increase the GAG ​​(performance rating) of your horse through appropriate selection of races and successful riding. If your horse starts in a race, you can place bets.
 
Tip: Beginners should definitely read the information in the 'Galloping Info' directory on the Derby disk in order to be informed about the terms of the cantering sport. Only one (!) simulation can be played at a time, i.e. when a new simulation starts, all old data is deleted. The data from a simulation is automatically saved continuously. The disk's write protection must never be active. The program must always be exited properly and never trigger a reset during the simulation game.

449008.overview: A train station management simulation for one player requiring strategy and timing created by Ashely Greenup using AmigaBASIC and released in 1995.

449080.overview: The English translation of the title is "The Caravan of the Seventh Dynasty". To play this game, you should have a working knowledge of German. You find yourself wandering around in a lonely desert after meeting somebody called "Gi Mando". you have received a task from "Gi Mando" before the start of the game and is now found in a lonely desert. Graphics illustrate the text.  The game is divided into five different worlds (In the Desert, In Bubble Gum Land, Casa Extasa, At the Fair, In Banana Land). At the end of each part you receive a password to get to the next world. The Amiga version was released again in 2004 on the games collection, Amiga Classix 4.

449105.overview: A freeware Polish Arkanoid type game created by Andrzej Radecki of Blue Data and released in 1992. Remove all the bricks, it is as simple as that. A remastered version of the game came out in 2024 from the Polish Amiga Floppy Preservation Group. The game features 40 levels in total of which the first 10 have added life bonuses.

449109.overview: A German advergame published by the Sparkasse a credit institute using characters from the KNAX comics. These are some kind of mascots and the magazines are given for free as they are used to rise awareness of the Sparkasse especially by their future customers. The comics usually deal with the struggle between the residents of the village Knax (the good ones) and their opponents located in castle Fetzenstein (the bad ones) who are usually trying to steal the villagers money. In this game the player can select between Didi and Dodo which are basically the main protagonists of the comics. The goal is to collect all the coins on a 6x6 squares playfield. To make it more difficult the player is chased by one of five possible members from castle Fetzenstein. It is possibly to drop up to five traps per level which slow the opponent down while the traps left at the end of a level award the player bonus points. The remaining time of the time limit does the same. In later levels there are special squares which can only be crossed for a few times or slow the player down for example. Although the opponent is faster then the protagonist only he can leave the playfield to appaer on the opposite side much like in Pac-Man. The game features a Highscore list.

449603.overview: A German-language, game-show quiz game, based on the former German TV show on RTL Television. This is basically The Price is Right, in German the Price is Hot created by Thomas Lopatic aka Dr. Nobody/HQC in 1991. Up to four participants in the game show guess the selling prices of various products and whoever comes closest has the chance to win the product. In other phases of the game show, cash prizes are handed out.

449647.overview:
Dungeon Adventure concludes Level 9's Middle Earth lineage of fantasy interactive fiction games (later reprogrammed with graphics in Jewels of Darkness). The player is searching for magical treasures within the Demon Lord's fortress, after his defeat in Adventure Quest.

There are over 200 specific locations, including rooms within the tower and outdoor locations to navigate en route. Objects range from a coffin and a giant belt to nasty images and a packing case; also watch out for Orcs, Dwarves and other creatures. The parser's vocabulary contains all the standard terms - EXAMINE, TAKE, OPEN and FILL for example.

449648.overview: Dr Xes, a supposed therapeutic piece of software where you type your problems and receive automated answers. This game tries to simulate artificial intelligence, similar to ELIZA or ALTER EGO on the C64. The 'virtual shrink' will react depending on the answers you give. TRIVIA: Try to read the doctor's last name backwards!

449650.overview: An AMOS based action\multi-genre mini-game collection from Sargon aka Roger North. Was distributed on AMOS PD disk 386 and is for one player. A compilation of single player games revamped in AMOS including The Crusher (a hangman style game), Hail of Barbs, The Minefield, Demon Driver, Satanic Surround (Lightcycle), The Caterpillar (snake) and Trail Blazer  (snake variant) mini-games.

449680.overview:
Program design by Susan Christie Thomas. Amiga conversion by Dean Brown. Educational title features mouse-keyboard control and a quit back to WB option. Discover: U. S. History and Geography is an education and entertainment game, developed and published by Maverick, which was released in 1989. These games were released individually and as part of a compilation and could be played by one or two players. 
 
This complete package contains History and Geography programs. Discover the Union States, Presidents and notable people and events in History. Then test your knowledge of areas, population and distances. (Ages 8 to adult)

449683.overview:
A German-language text adventure with still pictures created by Michael Mazur of Vertec Design exclusively published by Berliner Spielekiste SK #172 but later released as freeware. It is based on the solo adventures of the “Black Eye” and the role-playing playbooks "Lone Wolf". Anyone who has one of these and has knowlege of both game systems, you can in principle start playing immediately. 

At the top left of the screen is the status display of the player. A description follows. 
 
Power: The player's life force.At the beginning always 30 points.
Courage: The player's courage. Is between 6 and 13 points.
Skill: Shows how skillful the player is can behave. Is between 6 and 13 points.
Attack: The player's attack power.Lies between 2 and 4 points.
Defense: The defense force (has nothing to do with vitamin C to do) of the player.Is between 2 and 4 points.
Gold: Number of gold pieces the player has. 

To the right of the whole thing there is an icon bar with three symbols. With the first you can see the items you are carrying and view objects. The floppy disk symbol is used to load and save Scores. The last symbol is to exit the game.

On the top right of the screen are the graphics of the places you go to in the game. The lower part of the game is reserved for the text. Man gets a description of the room and below a few choices that you can easily use by Clicking on the mouse to execute it

449684.overview: A German language adventure with multiple choice selections for the player and still pictures to set the scene.  The Game was first Published in the Amiga Joker Magazine as Joke Role-Playing game in the Reader Service. Later republished in Germany by Berliner Spielekiste SK # 369.

449746.overview: An Amiga freeware game by Antti Siirtola, released "artificial intelligence v1.00" on 2/7/1997. The game was inspired by Microsoft Hearts and follows the same rules. The game is RTG capable and was written in C. This was a reader Game from Amiga Format CD 18.

449747.overview: A freeware puzzle game from Rio Spiege of Internal Excile Designs in 1996. The goal of the game is to smash blocks of the same color together making them disappear. Gravity can also be used to join them together, which is especially useful to remover 3 or more bricks.

449750.overview: A two player shooter created by Chris Padgett aka Zathoros and released as PD in 1996. A split screen, 2-D, game where two cowboys are gunning for each other. While primary a two-player game, it does have a "primitive" single player mode. You can set the starting ammo, reloads, heals available, obstacles, you can set the background and gore level.

449751.overview: The original Dictator, also by Steven Pugh came out a year earlier, this game is an update and upgrade all in one. Both are strategy games for up to 4 human players or up to 6 players with mix of human and compy players, both freeware and both written in GFA Basic. Distributed in SB-Soft 130-684 and by The Assassins.

449757.overview: A freeware, single player Minesweeper puzzle variant game created with AMOS by Sylvain Zangiacomi in 1997. Use logic and deduction to determine where the mines are and mark them successfully to win. It has built in sound voice files and instructions in French.

449765.overview: A freeware game by John Girvin from 1992 using GFA BASIC. In this workbench game you are The Doctor (who?), and you are trapped on the Dalek planet. your only hope of escape is to destroy all the Daleks on each level. The genocide is made possible by the Dalek's total stupidity. To kill them by crashing them into each other, since their reflexes are too slow for them to stop themselves. Daleks exist only to kill you and will always move towards your current position, use this knowledge to direct them into each other and into other ex-Dalek wrecks. You have at your disposal a limited amount of Teleport, Sonic Screwdriver uses and the Last Stand.

449773.overview: Dicey! is a Yahtzee clone and is the best implementation we've seen yet. — By Bill Mullen & Mike Monastero, released commercially in 1990, was part of the DevWare FunDisk 024 Strategy Games release by DevWare and also by CAM.

449778.overview: An AMOS based puzzle\memory game created by John Snowball of Darkside PD in 1999. Try to remember and match the tile the computer picks for you. Several levels of difficulty.

449795.overview:
An Emerald Mine\Boulderdash game created by Denis Forde with the Emerald Mine Editor and published commercially by the Emerald Mine Club in 1996. The player is deep down in a cave and has to collect emeralds and diamonds while evading monsters - and the laws of gravity, which have the annoying habit of squishing him with huge rocks if he happens to stand beneath one as it falls down.

The game also has a two-player mode where two people can rid caves of their valuables at the same time.

450057.overview: Digger 95 is a German-language BoulderDash clone created by Degra Software and released in 1998.

450058.overview:
An unusual platform game from Tim Sycamore, released as freeware in 1992. Guide the talking fish around the level using:
Q = walk left
W = walk right
P = Jump

450068.overview: A Tetris clone for workbench play by Daniel Westerberg aka Deniil 715 in 2002. You can choose 4 different sizes of playing field, optional pieces, edit piece color for instant recognition, and the ability to save up to 100 games. A v3.0 promises multiiplayer options and 21 new pieces and a Beta version of the game was available.

450071.overview: The second in a series of over 20 BoulderDash games by Skippy and NoelDerDash, created with the Emerald Mine Editor and sold commercially by the Emerald Mines Club of Australia in 1992 (with later releases in 1993). Over 80 levels of fun in the this version! Most levels by Skippy and the remaining levels by NoelDerDash.

450089.overview:
Die is everything you have ever dreamed of . It takes two player duels in a new dimension on amiga. The basic idea is very simple (two little men trying to kill each other), but behind the curtain you'll find what it really has to offer. 
- 128 color graphics + cool copper-color slides. 
- 2 layers (front and background layer) 
- special effects , like parallax clouds and water 
- over 300 frames of quality animation 
- levels supporting background animations 
- interactive objects, like teleports, doors and ladders 
- 20 deadly weapons + other things to collect (shield, health pack, gravity belt, speed etc..) 
- different game modes like rob-a-flag -mode 
- you can customize gravity, max.health etc. 
- you can create your own levels and now... the heart of the game: 
- all weapons are made of pixels (like in turboraketti and roketz) This great pixel routine supports homing bullets, pixels with gravitation and special abilities. 
- up to 200 pixels on screen at once
 - The game runs at maximum speed on my A1200+030+fastmem And i think it runs with full speed on A1200+fastmem, if you turn some special effects off. 
- and for the last, but not least.... the game is FREEWARE! 

My only request is that you send me some feedback if you like or hate this game happy killing, naama/Naamahaukat DIE requires an AGA Amiga and about 1 meg of free chipmem, but fastmem is strongly recommended. I have only tested DIE with my A1200 030 and on a basic A1200, so i don't really know whether it works on other machines. On a basic A1200 it's slow (25fps), but i think that fastmem will add some speed, so if you have an A1200 with only some extra fastmem let me know how the game runs on it. tip: If the game is slow, try turning off 2d-layer,special effects and backround anims. (you can also try turning vwait off, but not recommended if you suffer from epilepsy If it's still slow, buy an accelerator 

"Game controls" You can control characters with joystick or keyboard. Joystick: up/down - change shooting angle left/right - walk left/right up + left/right - jump left/right fire - shoot Keyboard: arrows + shift Jetpack Controls: up/down - accelerate left/right - change direction/shooting angle fire - shoot In ladders: Hold down fire and move with joystick or arrow keys. (note! you can't shoot when you are in ladders) To open/close a door, just go on top of the button and press fire. easy? @endnode @node options "Game options" When you go to the options menu you'll find a bunch of options to choose from. (the menu is controlled via mouse in case you haven't noticed In some options right mouse button is used to cycle value backwards. for example the scenario button. L.mouse for next scenario and r.mouse for previous

450104.overview:
With Desert Racing of Bardos we'll show you a racing game that you have never senn on the Amiga before. Use different components for your car depending on your money, drive through amazing animated landscapes and bring your AGA Amiga to boil. In the single or multiplayer modes you'll not only have the possibilty of tuning the performance but also other things.....

We take the meaning of tuning very strict because the you will need the different weapon systems to succeed in the dirty desert races.

To get into the pleasure of Desert Racing of Bardos your Amiga has to be equipped with an AGA chipset or a graphicsboard. A 68040 is minimum. 1,5MB ChipRAM and 32 MB FastRAM are the requirements but more is always better.

Get Desert Racing of Bardos and experience an exiting arcade racing game without getting envious to the PC world....  
 
A game for one or two players, written in Blitz BASIC. Coding by Ralf Schmidt.

450299.overview: This  game can be played by SIX players, each one of whom has his or her personal  game  displayed  on the screen.  The aim is for each player to find  the  exit  and go on to the following level.  This is a novel idea which Mark says came from an old Electron title. Distributed in APD381 in 1991 as freeware, this AMOS based game was created by Mark Potter.

450300.overview: A freeware fighting game for two players created by Dragon Software in 1992. From Australia Take out your agression in this two player Karate game where you have to kick the sense out of your opponent. Two-player simulation of the Far Eastern martial art "KickBoxing". The two "athletes" are animated to kick, punch and do other actions using joysticks . The higher score (for hits) is decisive for victory.

450301.overview: A freeware, vertically scrolling space shooter created by The Shadow of Darkhorse in 1992. A tough Astralian shoot'em up where, like just in reality you only get one life.

450303.overview: A game that can be played against the computer or another human for increased difficulty.  Each  player has his own screen to follow the wizard's progress as he goes around collecting herbs to make spells. A game created in AMOS by  	Mark Potter and released as freeware in 1993. Was distributed on APD 461 along with Frust, another of Mark Potter's games.

450305.overview: A AMOS, freeware based homebrew racing game for one person created by Dave Cherrington and distributed by SKE in 1992. In the game you control a ball and must roll around the track without touching the walls.

450382.overview: A freeware AMOS shooter from Dragon Software in 1993. This game is not the 1987 game of the same name from Psygnosis, but they both share the fact that they are crosshairs shooters, set in space. This one is more of a personal level shooter, instead of from the perspective of shooting from a ship.

450563.overview:
Normally simple Polish language puzzle game for one or two players, which can be compared to an old card game called "matching pairs" or something like that. It involves choosing. This version is for a whopping 10 player! 

Players draw two cards, alternating, so that they constitute a pair. The game ends when all pairs are revealed. If this is difficult, you can choose the version of the game with questions, i.e. after discovering the pair, you have to answer the question. The topics of the questions are comprehensive and cover areas such as science and music. geography, sports, mathematics, chemistry. Computer science and trivia. There are two bomb cards hidden among the entire deck. Taking one of them causes you to lose half your points, but two bombs are treated as a normal pair.  I will also add that the game has a great quality. What deserves attention is the sound samples of human speech used throughout the game.

451754.overview: Good a tempest type game with a mix of a 3D and vector graphics look. Stop the enemies from getting to the outer ring on 3 areas, The player must prevent these enemies from taking over the lower parts or touching the surfaces - through targeted constantly by enemies and their shots. In the second level there are four areas, on the third there are five, so it gets more difficult every time. Additionally there are three levels of chosen difficulty to choose from.

451756.overview: A game of deduction and cunning! An AMOS based dominoes board game from Silicon Sircus in 1995.

451757.overview: A shareware puzzle game for one or two players, created by Manfred Kopp and released in 1992. It is a game played on a 10x10 board where the goal is to set as many tiles on the board as possible. there are 100 different color combinations for a single tile, and rules you must determine for where tiles may be placed in relation to others.

451758.overview: Doctor Who: The Quiz Game was created in AMOS by Nigel Ellis in 1994 and released as freeware. And has brain teasers for all levels of Whovians. It is a simple multiple choice quiz game based on Doctor Who. It features questions about all the doctors from the 1st doctor until the 7th doctor and the adventures they were involved with. Bits of extra information will accompany many of the questions.

451759.overview: A game very much like a 15 slider puzzle, except you are recreating the dumbell parts into a coherent picture. A puzzle game by David Cole in 1989, published by Wicked Software as Shuff-It.

451764.overview: In most non-English languages (except those that acquired the game from English speakers), checkers is called dame, dames, damas, or a similar term that refers to ladies. So this is a freeware checkers game distributed by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) and written in C.

451766.overview:
A game to train your photographic mind. Coded in Amos Pro by Volker Stepprath of Testaware and distributed by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) in 1992.  Memory game for especially experienced brain acrobats. First the player gets a 10 x 10 field large table shown. Of the 100 small ones shown Tables are missing, for example. 4 pieces. Now the first picture and the complete 100 panels appear again. Now the player has to find the positions those in the model were missing the pieces. 
Again a game against the clock; but 10 times you can Ask for help. After each level there is a level pass word.

451767.overview: Dark Star from J. Lehn-Hauser is one of the easier SEUCK games for one or two players, crated in 1990.  Distributed by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) and by Bavarian. A vertically scrolling shooter, take out the space helicopters.

451768.overview: A German-language, freeware puzzle named after Santa Claus - who has not ever in his youth drawn the house of Nicholas? Here it will be a little heavier: on each side there is still a roof add! Try to draw the house with four gables (red lines) without any offsets and without going over a line twice. Game was written in GFA Basic.

451770.overview: A crosshairs shooter that is reminiscent of Missile Command that replaces crosshair blasts for missiles as you protect your city and infrastructure from the alien attack. A game created with AMOS by David Boucher of Ripoffware Software Productions in 1991.

451780.overview: A shareware game created by Robert Paauwe of SolfStar Software in 1986. An action game of strategy and luck. Move around the screen trying to get the Daleks to crash into one another whilst avoiding them.  You move one step, the Daleks move one step.  You have one sonic screwdriver per level and can teleport, but teleporting can place you anywhere and often is in a place of doom.

451781.overview: A freeware AMOS adventure game in German by Andreas Wiencke, released in 1994.

451782.overview: A freeware naval shooter by Bernd Schwarzmann, crated in 1995 usin C++.

451783.overview: Simple Software (Alan James) gave us this freeware update of Blitz for the Vic-20 revamped and dressed up pretty for the Amiga in 1995. A plane flies across a single-screen cityscape at a steady speed. When it reaches the edge of the screen, it wraps to the other side at a lower altitude, with its speed increasing each pass. The player drops bombs from the plane, and each bomb removes one or more segments of the structure it hits. As the plane descends, it risks colliding with remaining buildings. The level is complete when all buildings are destroyed, and the plane has descended safely to the bottom of the screen.

451784.overview:
DieserZug is a "snake" game where you control a train collecting ever more cars spread around the screen. Each car has a different value affecting how much your train grows. If you collide with the walls or with yourself, the game is over.

The game is system-friendly and runs as a small divertissement on the Workbench screen. There are three speed settings.

451785.overview:
Dimono is a freeware puzzle game by Arnold Schommer in C and distributed by Franz in 1994. The game can be run from the workbench. 

Dimono is a captivating puzzle game which challenges players with its unique strategic depth and puzzle-solving elements. Set in a top-down perspective, Dimono offers a minimalist design that focuses on mental challenge rather than graphical flair. Players navigate through various levels, each presenting a new set of puzzles that require logical thinking and quick decision-making. The simplicity of its interface, combined with the complexity of its puzzles, makes Dimono a standout game. 

The main objective in Dimono is to manipulate different shaped tiles to complete specific patterns or sequences. As players progress, the puzzles increase in complexity, introducing new types of challenges and obstacles. This gradual escalation in difficulty keeps the gameplay exciting and mentally stimulating. Dimono’s ability to blend basic graphical elements with profound puzzle structures offers a nostalgic yet fresh experience for all lovers of classic puzzle games.

451786.overview: Released as a coverdisk in 1990, this card game from Tom McHugh and Howard J. Anstedt is a two-deck solitaire game. Object of the game is to build cards by suit, in ascending order on all four aces and in descending order on all four kings. The left build column initially contains four aces. Each ace is to be built upon with the next card in

451787.overview: The first in a series of over 20 BoulderDash games by Skippy, created with the Emerald Mine Editor and sold commercially by the Emerald Mines Club of Australia in 1991 (with later releases in 1992 and 1993). 80 levesl fo fun in the primary version, though there were two versions of the game and one release under the name Down Under Mines 1.

451788.overview: The eleventh in a series of over 20 BoulderDash games by Skippy and Wily E., created with the Emerald Mine Editor and sold commercially by the Emerald Mines Club of Australia in 1992 (with later releases in 1993). Over 80 levels of fun in the this version! the first 59 levels by Skippy and the remaining levels by Wily E.

451789.overview: The third in a series of over 20 BoulderDash games by Skippy and NoelDerDash, created with the Emerald Mine Editor and sold commercially by the Emerald Mines Club of Australia in 1992 (with later releases in 1993). Over 80 levels of fun in the this version!

451790.overview: A text adventure game with selectable answers where you can visit different bars and pubs, gaining points depending on the answers you give and behaviors that you entertain in various circumstances. It actually gets pretty demented in a fun way, with a focus on heavy drinking, machismo, bar fights and other street-smart themes. The humor is pretty lowbrow, but still entertaining. A freeware AMOS game from Roland Acton in 1994.

451791.overview: A freeware 1993 puzzle game created by David Faught. Mod music files could be played using Teijo Kinnunen's mod player, which can be called by the game. Use the 8, 4, 6 and 2 keys on the numeric keypad to move through the maze shown on top. Use of the zero key will exit the program. There are 2 mazes, one red and one blue on top of each other. The mazes are different from each other and different every time you play. You start at the left end of both mazes and have to get to the exits on the right end of both mazes. About every 40 moves or so, using the magic of dual playfields, the top and bottom mazes are swapped.

451792.overview: A freeware AMOS based shooter in the style of Moon Buggy by Alfred Messler in 1992 and released by Spielekiste (Berlin PD). it may also contain the first appearance of the Flying Spaghetti Monster (FSM) and his noodly appendages.

451806.overview: A freeware, German-language, matchup fighting game by Michael Mazur created in 1993 and for up to 4 players.

451819.overview: Da Cool Quiz is a quiz game about the Amiga itself and to some degree the surrounding community and shorthand terms used by Amigans and Miggy's alike. This would be published in The 'The Best of Airsoft Softwair' CD-ROM, which was released just in time for the Home Electronics World '99 in Cologne. This would also be republished by APC&TCP.

451854.overview:
This is a porting I have completely rewritten from my code for Apple ii to Amiga of the Game Doctor Say, I have built.
To play follow the Amiga voice instructions and write your answer with keyboard and press return every time.

This game is born by my idea, after reading a BING article who spoke that a good chatbot doctor could not be made, so I  thought why not try with a game. From a game can born a bigger project if someone develop it with a good programming team.

Inside the D folder there is the source code DoctorSay. The game was created in AMOS by Matteo Trevisan aka Toolkitman.

451855.overview: Likely intended to piggyback on the immense popularity of Jurassic Park, Dinosaurs One was the first in a two part series of games intended to edu-tain on the subject and timeline of dinosaurs. It was created by Chris Hill of Total Concepts and published by Central Licenseware Register in 1993. Essentially it is a slideshow of great dinosaur pictures with information about them and what was happening in the timeline during their lifespan.

451857.overview: Dungeon was originally written by the founders of Infocom, Inc. when they were at MIT, in the late 70's. this version has been ported to the Amiga by David Kinder. This is a version of Dungeon, which in turn is the Fortran version of Zork, an early mainframe text adventure game written by the founders of Infocom while at MIT. I've added a decent Amiga front-end in C rather than having it run via the CLI, but that's the only change from the original.

451992.overview: A puzzle game from Nick Christie, created in C and released as GPL2 Open Source. Version 1.1 was released on February 8th, 1994. It is a Taipei\Mahjong style game where accessible tiles can be removed in pairs. Winning can be done by removing all the tiles. Clicking on a free tile will indicate the number of that type of tile still available. A Mandelbrot set picture acts as the default background.

451998.overview: An AMOS based shareware game by C. Edward Stewart of Fly By Nite on the 12th of February of 1996. From version 2.0 onward the game supported multiplayer over a modem or similar connection. A full blown text adventure engine for head to head fighting or to allow you to explore many different worlds with different goals, you can cooperate with your remote partner or attack!

452189.overview: A board game aimed at youngsters from Denis Obriot using Blitz-BASIC in 1997. This game can be played on the workbench and represents a classic French board game of a race of horses. Supports French and English localizations.

452297.overview:
Doppelkopf is a 4 player, German language casino\card counting, trick taking card game by Jonasoft in 1998. Doppelkopf (German pronunciation: [ˈdɔpl̩kɔpf], lit. double-head), sometimes abbreviated to Doko, is a trick-taking card game for four players.

In Germany, Doppelkopf is nearly as popular as Skat, especially in Northern Germany and the Rhein-Main Region. Schafkopf, however, is still the preferred point-trick game in Bavaria. As with Skat and Bavarian Schafkopf there is a set of official rules, but numerous unofficial variants.

452298.overview: A shareware casino game created and published by Setephan Preuss and the final 2.2 version was released in 1998.

452308.overview: An AMOS based, French-language freeware game from Sylvain Zangiacomi, released in 1997. The game is somewhat in the style of WORMS or some of the artillery duel games except you are armed with boomerangs as your primary weapon. Movement is available and there are some bonus packages scattered around the single-screen level.

452755.overview:
DUEL is a remake of the classic cowboy/shootout games from Z80 machines that (a bit) predates the c64 era. Probably this is why hard to find an Amiga version.

You can move your guy up or down, throw grenades or use a shield and use a mouse to targetting. The game is not complicated and it can be a lot of fun  shooting your fellow Amiga user (Player_Vs_Player) into pieces sitting next to you. :) ..or you can fight against the computer (Player_Vs_CPU). 
 
For the creative ones:
If you can use Deluxe/Personal-Paint (or any equvivalent ) You can create new backgrounds and characters if you follow the "Example.txt" in the zip file.

454142.overview: A BoulderDash style game by Rudiger Werner, published in 1990 as shareware and created in GFA Basic. Avoid the chompers and gather all the treasure. It has level passwords to easily come back to where you left off and a level editor.

454351.overview: You play as a brave hero on a quest to enter the Dungeons of Doom and slay the Dark Lord. With your trusty weapons, armour and shield, you must navigate the maze of dungeons ahead and vanquish your foes. Collect bonus weapons, spells, treasures and find food to keep you from starving. The Dark Lord has sent hordes of monsters to stop you. Dungeonette is a hybrid of many games in reality and has some roots in Diablo for sure but also many others as a hack & slash dungeon crawler.

454933.overview: In Dogi, the goal is to collect various fruits and avoid obstacles and enemies. A Christmas platformer from Amiten Games for Christmas 2024. Dogi is a dog that lives in a wonderful place, full of lights and lots of fruits and candies. But one day the inhabitants of the wonderland have become selfish and guard all the food. Your mission is to collect all the food and distribute it amongst the kids who do not have enough. Once you have all the fruit on the level you can move on to the next one.

454938.overview: This is a single player turn based Strategy WW2 war game against 3 different lvls of AI enemy. At the moment there is 12 battlefields with Three lvls of gameplay and you need to win All 36 battles to win the campaign to see the end sequence.

455909.overview:
After reading the background story there will be a GUI that should be pretty much self explaining.
There are buttons for every possible action, and some message strings in the main window.

457398.overview: The Game is text/graphical adventure that takes the player into a strange and upsetting world. The game consist of original graphics and music, and lets the player enter a realm of strange machines, puzzles and twists in the many locations that exists for the player to explore.

459339.overview: I was a huge fan of the Dizzy games on the C64, after a friend introduced me to Dizzy 1 and 2. As soon as he showed me how to kill all the enemies, suddenly the whole game opened up, and I beat it over and over. For me, Dizzy 1 is still the best.

459775.overview: The game is a mini-game in which you have to dodge the gray balls with a red ball for as long as you can. These increase in number over time, making the game more difficult and inevitably leading to a collision. The longer you last, the more points you get.

459896.overview: Doom, The Ultimate Doom,Doom II: Hell on Earth, TNT: Evilution, The Plutonia Experiment

461982.overview:
Death Square is a strategy game for two players and is played on a square board with 8 squares per side. At the beginning the blue and red pieces fill the board entirely except for the 16 central squares. This last area is called Death Square.

At the start of each game, players take turns moving their pieces into the Death Square. The person who manages to remove all of their opponent's pieces from the Death Square by jumping over them wins.

Of course, multiple jumps are allowed as in the game of Checkers. To load the program, simply double click on the icon. After loading, the chessboard with the Death Square highlighted is displayed. Players make their moves with the mouse. Pressing the Escape key exits the game.

The red player always moves first. The color of the mouse pointer indicates the game turn.

Published in AmigaMagazine OnDisk #24 in June of 1991.

461986.overview:
Destructive Poker is a solitaire poker simulator with some interesting features. To start the game, select "New" from the "Game" menu; you begin with 40 credits, and for each hand, a wager is deducted—calculated by adding the number of wildcards in the deck to the number of allowed card exchanges. To adjust your bet, select the "Bet" option. Naturally, increasing the number of exchanges (up to a maximum of 3) or wildcards (up to 8) boosts your chances of getting a winning hand, though it costs more per wager. The "Shuffle" button allows you to reshuffle the deck; if luck isn't on your side, a good shuffle might turn the game around. Once you have decided on your bet, press "Done" to be dealt your cards. After choosing which cards to swap, simply select them and press "Done" again. Cards marked as "Joker" or "Extra" act as wildcards, and the computer automatically assigns them the value that yields the highest score. When the exchanges are complete, a dialog box appears to announce your score.

Published in the June 1997 edition of AmigaMagazine OnDisk #90.

462689.overview: Doom8088 is a port for PCs with a 16-bit processor like an 8088 or a 286, and with MDA, CGA, EGA, VGA or MCGA graphics.

465441.overview: Amiga port of Dig Dug 2 arcade

468244.overview:
Baboon City sleeps beneath its neon glow…
Until an alien invasion turns its citizens into mindless blobs.

471077.overview: Dunjons is a small turn-based dungeon hack/slash made using AmiBlitz3 for the Retro Programmers Inside (RPI) and Phaze101 Maze Game Jam 2026.

471923.overview: Port of Double Dragon for Amiga, Requires a 3-button joystick, CD32 pad, or the keyboard.

474409.overview: Transformed into a luminous energy creature, you drift through abandoned underground laboratories filled with machines, traps and remnants of a forgotten catastrophe.

480174.overview: This is a retro-style illustrated text adventure game in the format of a horror short story. You play the part of a young gentleman, Oswald Stanley, travelling to visit an old college friend on a fine summer's evening at the height of the Victorian era.  As the night progresses, events take a sinister turn with the emergence of a murderous evil spirit. What follows will chill Oswald to the very marrow, but will you be able to guide him safely through the night?

480753.overview: A gothic interactive adventure for Commodore Amiga, inspired by Bram Stoker's classic novel.

481132.overview:
Dizzy Gems is a match 3 or more columns style game created for the Commodore Amiga using AMOS Professional 2 & Deluxe Paint 4 for the graphics.

Drop columns of three gems into the playfield, rotate and position them, and create matches horizontally, vertically & diagonally. Clear gems, trigger chain reactions and build your score as the game gradually gets faster.

The game can be controlled using either the keyboard or a joystick. Press P to pause the game and M to toggle the music on or off.

Crack and destroy those pesky Stone Gems with exploding TNT Gems, build up your score, and try your best to knock The Creator off the number one spot on the leaderboard!

For the Commodore Amiga using AMOS Professional 2 & Deluxe Paint 4 for the graphics.

481302.overview: The Doodies are rising, soldier, and Squad Alpha is all that stands between them and a clean getaway. 482016.overview:

Enter a dark future where speed is everything.

Race through rain-soaked neon cities, elevated highways, underground tunnels and industrial landscapes in a futuristic anti-gravity racing game developed for classic Commodore Amiga computers.

482035.overview:
An addictive puzzle-platformer brought to the Commodore Amiga 500!

Deadlock – Amiga Edition is a port of the original Windows game created by winterbeak.

Combining platforming and puzzle-solving, Deadlock challenges you to think ahead, plan your moves and find a way through increasingly tricky levels. With 80 levels to solve, you'll need both logic and precision to overcome every obstacle.

482897.overview: The original is more like Dungeon Master than Doom and moves in steps between fixed standing points and fixed facings. Death Mask 3D renders the same levels using a first-person 3D engine using the original's graphics. The idea is to keep the feel close to the original game but in 3D, so it's more Wolfenstein 3D than Doom.
